docs.title: Coupled Modal Narrative Engine
docs.text:
CMNE Workbench is a local desktop instrument for drafting a bounded fictional scene, tracking what characters and readers can know, and producing an offline prose passage from a discourse plan. It separates story (what happens) from discourse (the order and form in which a reader encounters it). Its Mara and Len sample compares four kinds of change in Mara's understanding.

Implementation scope

This site documents the 2026-10-21 local implementation checkpoint. The workbench has a Tauri/React interface and a Python sidecar. The seeded sample produces four deterministic passages of about 800 words and three matched offline composition variants per condition for a blinded study dry run. An optional JSON adapter bridge supports recorded and replayed model calls; no external vendor is bundled or human study completed. Pages mark remaining gate work explicitly.

docs.title: One scene, two orders
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Fixture: actors, objects, initial facts] --> B[Story events: what happens]
    B --> C[Discourse acts: what is told]
    C --> D[Scene packet]
    D --> E[Offline realizer]
    E --> F[Passage and findings]
    B --> G[Six replay projections]
    C --> G
    G --> D

Example. In story time, Len repairs a chair before he leaves. In telling time, the reader meets the rocking chair after he leaves and learns about the repair later. A later event can change Mara's interpretation of that earlier repair without changing the original event.

docs.title: Documentation set
docs.text:
• The user manual is task-based. It follows the numbered scenarios S-01 through S-13 and uses labeled information blocks so a reader can find a procedure, rule, or explanation quickly.
  • The design section explains the implemented state, domain model, processes, storage, and gaps from the target SRS.
  • The API section covers the Python package, CLI, JSON-RPC sidecar, contracts, errors, and Tauri bridge.

The longer target specifications remain in the repository's _design/ folder. This site describes the running application and identifies design goals that have not yet shipped.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text:
The Python kernel is the source of narrative rules. The CLI calls it directly. The desktop UI calls it through Tauri's rpc_call, which relays to a line-framed JSON-RPC sidecar. The sidecar and GUI use the same project storage.

flowchart LR
  CLI --> Kernel[Python cmne kernel]
  React --> Tauri[Tauri rpc_call]
  Tauri --> Sidecar[cmne-sidecar]
  Sidecar --> Kernel
  Kernel --> Files[(Project folder)]
Interface Use Python kernel Scripting and tests in the same Python process CLI Create, run, and inspect a graph from a terminal JSON-RPC Full project, draft, graph, run, and export operations Data contracts Event fields, formula syntax, validation, errors Tauri bridge Frontend to sidecar command boundary

Protocol version is 1.0; event schema and reducer version are 2, while project metadata format remains version 1. Methods returning errors do not mutate sealed history unless explicitly described. See the storage design for the on-disk model.

docs.title: Command-line interface
docs.text:
Install the package in a virtual environment, then run cmne --help. Add --json before the command for machine-readable success and error objects. Success exits 0; a domain or input error exits 2 and includes a code, cause, field path, and corrective action.

Command Effect create PATH [--name NAME] [--sample] Create a project and optional Mara/Len sample validate-contract FILE Validate a JSON narrative contract replay PATH [--branch ID] Replay six projections and hashes fork PATH SEQUENCE NAME [--branch ID] Create an independent branch and draft suffix apply-revision PATH C0\|C1\|C2\|C3 Inspect a seeded condition's revision state plan-discourse PATH FILE [--branch ID] Atomically seal an acts array from JSON packet PATH [--branch ID] Build a filtered scene packet realize PATH [--branch ID] [--variant 0\|1\|2] Realize and check deterministic prose check PATH FILE [--branch ID] Check a UTF-8 prose file against the packet trace PATH TARGET [--query TYPE] Trace an event, actor belief, reader inference, model change, or run exposure run PATH [--branch ID] [--variant 0\|1\|2] Save a run and rejected-candidate findings propose PATH [--branch ID] --model-manifest FILE Save diagnostic model proposals outside canon accept-proposal PATH PROPOSAL_ID [--branch ID] Validate and seal a stored proposal graph PATH [--branch ID] [--lens LENS] Read a lens graph analysis-plan PATH FILE Save or amend the fixed study plan study-generate PATH Save three matched template variants for C0–C3 study-metrics PATH [--branch ID] Read blocking and descriptive structural measures study-ablations PATH [--branch ID] Read seven analysis-only ablation descriptions study-realize-ablations PATH [--branch ID] Save seven controlled ablation passages and checker findings export-evaluation PATH [--seed N] Write randomized public passages and a separate private key responses-import PATH STUDY_ID FILE Atomically validate and import evaluator responses report PATH STUDY_ID Save and print a descriptive study report decision-packet PATH STUDY_ID Save a hashed review packet with study, structural, and ablation evidence

Example:

source .venv/bin/activate
cmne create /tmp/cmne-example --sample
cmne --json replay /tmp/cmne-example
cmne study-generate /tmp/cmne-example
cmne analysis-plan /tmp/cmne-example plan.json
cmne export-evaluation /tmp/cmne-example --seed 33

analysis-plan must precede export. The CLI accepts only JSON imports; it does not execute YAML tags. See Prepare a blinded evaluation for the plan and response fields. Long CLI runs are synchronous; the desktop sidecar offers background run polling and cancellation between conditions.

run and propose also accept --adapter-mode record|replay, --adapter-command EXECUTABLE, --model-manifest FILE, --max-calls, --max-tokens, optional --max-cost-micros, and --allow-data-transfer. The default run mode remains template. The model adapter contract explains the JSON protocol, privacy gate, cassette, and budget behavior.

docs.title: Data contracts and errors
docs.text:
All documents are JSON-compatible. IDs are strings. Basis-point values are integers in 0..10000. Validators return a copy with defaults and, for fixture/contract, a content_hash.

The runtime shape definitions are in src/cmne/contracts.py. scripts/export_schemas.py generates schema/cmne.schema.json and app/src/generated/contracts.ts; CI checks that both match the Python definitions. Semantic checks such as access and disclosure grounding remain in the kernel validators. JSON imports reject duplicate keys and nonfinite values.

docs.title: Fixture and contract
docs.text:
{
  "actors": [{"id":"mara","name":"Mara"},{"id":"len","name":"Len"}],
  "entities": [{"id":"chair","name":"Chair","kind":"object","motif":true}],
  "initial_facts": [],
  "style": {"focalizer":"mara","distance":"close"}
}

A fixture requires exactly two actors, each with unique id and name. Entities need unique IDs and names. Optional initial facts and style feed replay. A new project uses actor_a and actor_b placeholders and no entities.

{
  "required_story_conditions": [],
  "forbidden_story_conditions": [],
  "facts_that_must_be_clear": [],
  "questions_that_must_remain_open": [],
  "prose_bounds": {"min_words":0,"max_words":1100},
  "strain_threshold_bp":6500,
  "strain_weights_bp":{"contradiction":2500,"unexplained":2000,"failed_prediction":2000,"repair_complexity":2000,"identity_goal":1500},
  "high_commitment_bp":7000,
  "repair_budget_bp":5000
}

Required and forbidden conditions may not overlap; a claim may not be both clear and open. Bounds must be ordered nonnegative integers. Strain weights must total 10,000 basis points. The run checks required story facts, selected grounding/voice rules, forbidden strings, and word bounds. Arbitrary open questions still require a reviewer or a project-specific rule.

docs.title: Story event payload
docs.text:
{
  "title":"Mara finds the note",
  "kind":"observation",
  "description":"A note lies beneath the bowl.",
  "actor_ids":["mara"],
  "entity_ids":["bowl"],
  "causal_parents":["evt_…"],
  "observed_by":["mara"],
  "access_path":"perception",
  "world_facts":["note_under_bowl"],
  "strain_components_bp":{"contradiction":2000,"unexplained":7000,"failed_prediction":4000,"repair_complexity":3000,"identity_goal":4000},
  "preconditions":[]
}

title is required. kind defaults to action and may be action, observation, utterance, recollection, decision, revision, or crisis. Causal parents must be earlier sealed event IDs. Observation requires observed_by and an access path of perception, testimony, or memory. New assessments use five strain_components_bp values; replay retains historical strain_bp for older sealed events. A crisis also needs crisis with observer, accessible evidence sequence, commitment, and repair cost. Optional interpretations have observer, model version, claim, and earlier targets; revisions preserve earlier records. belief_revision has status, confidence, and accessible evidence. modal_revision can add/remove constraints or scenarios; conceptual_revision records new concepts and a migration map. Generated proposals use source_kind: generated, proposal_id, and validator_id: cmne-command-validator-v2.

docs.title: Discourse act payload
docs.text:
{
  "title":"The note",
  "mode":"scene",
  "story_refs":["evt_…"],
  "text":"Under the bowl, a folded note waited.",
  "focalizer":"mara",
  "reveal":["note_under_bowl"],
  "cue":[],
  "withhold":[]
}

title is required. mode defaults to scene and also accepts summary, ellipsis, pause, memory, and repetition. Optional narrative_time, duration_weight_bp, salience_bp, and variant record telling choices. References must exist on the branch. Every revealed claim must occur in a referenced event's world_facts, unless hypothetical or unreliable is truthy. A claim already revealed cannot later be withheld. text becomes prose in the offline realizer.

docs.title: Formula AST
docs.text:
{"op":"and","operands":[
  {"op":"atom","predicate":"note_under_bowl"},
  {"op":"believes","observer_id":"mara","operands":[
    {"op":"atom","predicate":"len_left"}
  ]}
]}

Operators: atom, not, and, or, implies, necessarily, possibly, believes, suspends, in_scenario. atom takes predicate as a string or {name, arguments, polarity} object. not, the two modal operators, believes, suspends, and in_scenario take one operand; implies takes two; and/or take 2–16. believes/suspends require observer_id; in_scenario requires scenario_id. Maximum depth is 16 and maximum nodes 256. Evaluation returns true, false, or unknown (None) when the available state cannot decide a claim.

docs.title: Sealed event envelope
docs.text:
{"stream":"story","branch_id":"main","sequence":1,"schema_version":2,
 "payload":{"title":"…","source_kind":"authored"},"event_id":"evt_…","integrity_hash":"…"}

The event ID and integrity hash derive from the canonical envelope body. event_id is a stable prefix of the hash; integrity_hash is the full SHA-256 hex digest. Opening/reading a stream verifies both.

Version-1 story/discourse events are up-cast in memory with source_kind: authored; their stored lines and IDs remain unchanged. Newly sealed events use version 2. Project metadata remains format version 1.

docs.title: Common domain errors
docs.text:
Code Meaning / action E-FIXTURE-001, E-CONTRACT-001 Correct fixture cast/IDs or contract fields E-STORY-001, E-DISCOURSE-001 Correct event/act fields or references E-ACCESS-001 Add observer/access path or accessible belief evidence E-DISCLOSURE-001 Ground a reveal or fix withhold order E-FORMULA-001 Correct a bounded formula AST E-DRAFT-001, E-GRAPH-001 Fix draft fields/edges before seal E-STORE-001, E-SCHEMA-001 Stream failed integrity/schema validation; restore a valid backup E-LOCK-001 Close the other writer before opening the project E-RUN-001, E-EXPORT-001 Match branch/condition or run before export

The sidecar's error.data includes cmne_code, field_path, next_action, and cause for domain errors. command.submit can instead report a rejected command inside a successful RPC result.

The generated error catalog lists every current domain code, cause, and next action.

docs.title: Error catalog
docs.text:
Each domain error has a stable code, cause, and corrective action. The JSON-RPC error data also carries field_path when a validator can locate the offending input.

Code Message Cause Next action E-ACCESS-001 The observer cannot access this evidence. An observer lacks a declared route to evidence. Name the observer, access path, and accessible source event. E-ADAPTER-001 The model adapter is unavailable or invalid. A model adapter is unavailable or returned an invalid response. Use the offline template or check the adapter manifest and response contract. E-APPEND-001 The branch sequence is stale. The branch head changed since the caller read it. Reload the branch and submit against its current sequence. E-BELIEF-001 The belief revision is invalid. A belief revision is incomplete or out of range. Supply an observer, claim, status, confidence, and accessible evidence. E-BRANCH-001 The branch or fork point is invalid. The branch or fork point is invalid. Choose an existing branch and a sequence within its story history. E-BUDGET-001 The model budget is exhausted. A model run reached its call, token, or cost limit. Inspect the recorded spend and set a new explicit budget before retrying. E-CASSETTE-001 The model response cassette is missing or invalid. A recorded model response is missing or fails integrity validation. Record the canonical request first or restore its verified cassette. E-COMMAND-001 The command batch is invalid. The command has no supported event batch. Submit nonempty story or discourse payloads. E-CONCEPT-001 The conceptual revision is invalid. A conceptual revision lacks a model transition. Supply the observer, new concepts, and migration map. E-CONTRACT-001 The narrative contract is invalid. The narrative contract has a malformed or conflicting field. Correct the reported contract field and validate again. E-CRISIS-001 The model crisis is not eligible. A crisis gate lacks strain, commitment, failed repair, or accessible evidence. Supply accessible trigger evidence and a computed strain assessment above the threshold. E-DISCLOSURE-001 The disclosure is not grounded. A reveal is ungrounded or a withheld claim was already revealed. Reference a grounding story event or correct the disclosure order. E-DISCOURSE-001 The discourse act is invalid. A discourse act has an invalid field or reference. Correct the named act field and revalidate the draft. E-DRAFT-001 The draft cannot be saved or sealed. A draft is malformed or exceeds its limits. Fix the draft node or edge and preview again. E-EXPORT-001 There is no report to export. There is no saved run for the selected branch. Run the branch before exporting. E-FIXTURE-001 The fixture is invalid. The fixture cast or entity list is invalid. Define exactly two distinct actors and unique named entities. E-FORMULA-001 The formula is invalid or too large. The formula is malformed or exceeds its bounds. Use a supported operator and keep depth at most 16 and nodes at most 256. E-GRAPH-001 The graph connection is invalid. A graph connection is invalid or cyclic. Reconnect compatible nodes without a causal cycle. E-INPUT-001 The input file or path is unsafe or invalid. Input is missing, unsafe, oversized, or malformed. Use a valid JSON file inside the project and remove unsafe paths or tags. E-INTERPRET-001 The interpretation is invalid. An interpretation is missing provenance or targets the wrong event. Name the observer, model version, claim, and earlier target sequences. E-LOCK-001 The project writer lock prevents this change. Another writer owns the project or a lock needs review. Close the writer or explicitly clear a verified stale lock. E-MODAL-001 The modal revision is invalid. A modal revision has invalid observer or scenarios. Supply a known observer and a scenario list. E-MODEL-001 The modal model is inconsistent. Active modal constraints conflict or a ranked scenario lacks a revision basis. Remove the contradiction or cite a contradiction or revision event. E-PLAN-001 The analysis plan is missing or invalid. The analysis plan is absent or incomplete. Save a complete plan before exporting a blinded evaluation set. E-PRECOND-001 A command precondition does not hold. A command precondition is not true before the event. Inspect the preceding projection and revise the command or its evidence. E-PRIVACY-001 Model data transfer has not been enabled. Model data transfer was not enabled for this run. Enable transfer explicitly after reviewing the fixture and evaluator data. E-PROJECT-001 The project cannot be opened. The project path is invalid or no project is open. Open or create a valid project folder. E-PROSE-CAUSAL The prose contains an unsupported causal assertion. A causal sentence lacks accessible story evidence. Cite the story event that supports the cause or revise the sentence. E-PROSE-CLAIM The prose asserts a claim outside focal access. An asserted claim is outside focal access. Ground the claim in accessible evidence or mark it as hypothesis. E-PROSE-EARLY The prose reveals a claim too early. A withheld claim appears before its planned reveal. Move the claim to its reveal act or change the discourse plan. E-PROSE-ENTITY The prose introduces an unknown named entity. A named entity does not occur in the fixture. Add the entity to the fixture or remove the name. E-PROSE-FORBIDDEN The prose contains a forbidden assertion. A forbidden literal assertion appears in prose. Revise the authored text and run again. E-PROSE-PRIVATE The prose asserts private cognition outside focal access. Prose asserts another actor's private cognition. Recast it as a focalizer inference or provide licensed narration. E-PROSE-RESOLUTION The prose resolves an open question. Prose explicitly settles a contractually open question. Leave the question unresolved in this candidate. E-PROSE-WORDS The prose is outside its word bounds. The passage is outside the contract's word bounds. Revise discourse text or valid contract bounds and rerun. E-PROTO-001 The sidecar protocol is incompatible. The sidecar protocol version or request is incompatible. Use a matching app and sidecar version, then reconnect. E-RESPONSE-001 The evaluator response is invalid. An evaluator response is malformed or duplicates an existing response. Correct the named field and import the complete response batch again. E-RPC-001 The RPC method is unavailable. The requested RPC method is unknown or disallowed. Use a documented method name. E-RPC-INPUT The RPC parameters are invalid. RPC parameters are missing or malformed. Supply the documented parameter names and value types. E-RUN-001 The requested run cannot start. The requested condition does not match the branch. Select the branch for that condition or run the four sample branches in order. E-RUN-CONTRACT The story does not satisfy the contract. A required story fact is absent. Add the required fact to a valid story event and rerun. E-RUN-EMPTY The branch has no story events. The branch has no story events. Seal at least one story event. E-RUN-PLAN The branch has no telling plan. The branch has no discourse acts. Seal a discourse act tied to story. E-SAMPLE-001 The bundled sample could not be created. The bundled sample failed to initialize. Recreate the sample with a matching package version. E-SCHEMA-001 The schema version is unsupported. The data schema or version is unsupported. Use a supported schema or install a registered up-cast. E-STORE-001 The stored data failed integrity verification. Stored data failed integrity validation. Restore a verified backup; do not edit sealed streams by hand. E-STORY-001 The story event is invalid. A story event has an invalid field or causal reference. Correct the named event field and revalidate. E-STRAIN-001 The strain assessment is invalid. Strain weights or components are malformed. Provide five integer components and weights totaling 10000 basis points. E-STUDY-001 The study set is incomplete or invalid. The study set is incomplete or an identifier is invalid. Create three passing matched variants per condition and use a valid study ID. E-TRACE-001 The trace target is invalid. A trace target or observer is unknown. Use a committed event, run, claim, and observer for the query. E-UPCAST-001 The stored event cannot be up-cast. No migration path exists for a stored event version. Install a version with the required up-cast; preserve the stored bytes. E-VOICE-LENGTH A sentence violates the voice length rule. A sentence exceeds the voice length rule. Revise the sentence within the voice profile range. E-VOICE-PHRASE The prose contains a forbidden voice phrase. A forbidden voice phrase appears. Replace the phrase and check again.

E-RPC-INPUT covers malformed RPC parameters; a programming fault is returned as a JSON-RPC internal error and should be reported with the request method and application version.

docs.title: JSON-RPC sidecar
docs.text:
cmne-sidecar (or python -m cmne_sidecar.server) reads one JSON-RPC 2.0 request per input line and writes one response per output line. Keep one process open for a sequence of calls. app.hello must succeed before other methods; it accepts protocol major version 1 and returns version, schema, package, and lens names. Standard output is protocol only; diagnostics use standard error.

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"app.hello","params":{"protocol_version":"1.0"}}

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"protocol_version":"1.0","schema_version":2,"package_version":"…","lenses":["fixture","story","discourse","mind","provenance","motif","pipeline"]}}

docs.title: Project and validation
docs.text:
Method Parameters Result project.create path required; name, sample optional Project summary project.sample Optional path; defaults to Documents/CMNE/Mara and Len Opens or seeds sample; summary project.open path; optional read_only: true Project summary; read-only opens can coexist with a writer. A failed switch retains the previous project. Close before changing one project's access mode. project.clear_stale_lock path {cleared: true} only when a same-host lock owner is no longer running project.close — { "closed": true } project.get — Project summary fixture.validate / contract.validate fixture / contract Validated object with content_hash; no open project required fixture.get / contract.get — Current object fixture.save / contract.save fixture / contract Validated and saved object fixture.import / contract.import path to a JSON file Validated and saved object; unsafe paths, symlinks, YAML, and oversized files are refused

The summary has path, name, active_branch, branches, fixture, and contract. Saving a fixture or contract revalidates sealed story events and preconditions before replacing the file; an incompatible crisis threshold or other rule is rejected without changing the old contract. Neither save rewrites sealed events. Mutating methods refuse a read-only project.

docs.title: Branch, events, and graph
docs.text:
All branch-aware methods accept optional branch_id; omitted means the metadata's active branch, or main.

Method Other parameters Result branch.list — Branch metadata array branch.fork sequence required; name optional New branch_id, fork_sequence, draft_id branch.compare left, right Shared prefix, state-transition histories, changed interpretations, hashes events.read stream optional, default story Verified event array command.submit stream (story/discourse), either payload or nonempty payloads, optional expected_sequence accepted, emitted_events, rejected_reason, invariant results, before/after hashes graph.get lens, optional draft_id, sequence, discourse_index Lens graph envelope graph.validate_connection lens, source, target, kind, optional draft {accepted, reason} scrub.projection Optional sequence, discourse_index Six projections and hashes overlay.series / strain.series — Tension projection, including series trace.query node_id; optional query, actor_id, claim, model_version Event/proposal provenance, actor belief, reader inference, model change, or prose access

command.submit validates every payload in a same-stream batch before one atomic stream replacement. Later payloads can depend on earlier payloads in that batch. If any fails, none is appended. It returns accepted: false for a pre-commit narrative validation rejection. A storage or projection error after an append can return an RPC error even when the event committed; inspect events.read before retrying. Never infer rejection from a post-commit error.

docs.title: Drafts
docs.text:
Method Parameters Result draft.create Optional lens (story by default) Empty draft draft.get draft_id Draft JSON draft.list branch_id; optional lens (story by default) Recoverable drafts for that branch/lens, newest first draft.patch draft Saved draft JSON draft.compile_preview draft or draft_id {accepted, errors, count} draft.seal draft_id {accepted, errors, emitted_events, id_map} draft.delete draft_id {deleted: true}

A draft contains id, branch_id, lens, nodes, and edges. Node entries have id, title, and fields; edge entries have source, target, and kind (causes for story or refs for discourse). Preview and seal validate references, fields, and graph rules. Story draft seals in causal order; discourse draft seals in node ID order when no causal dependencies exist.

draft.list reads validated draft files on disk. The workbench uses it to recover a draft when its browser local-storage pointer is unavailable after a crash or reset.

docs.title: Run and export
docs.text:
Method Parameters Result packet.build / packet.get Optional branch_id Current computed packet; these do not read an archived packet by hash run.start Optional branch_id, conditions, variant_index, async: true Saved run(s), or {job_id, status, total} for a background run proposal.generate model_manifest; optional adapter_command, adapter_mode, budget, allow_data_transfer Diagnostic candidates and spend; canon unchanged proposal.accept proposal_id; optional branch_id Story event after ordinary validation run.status Optional branch_id or job_id Latest saved run, or background progress and completed runs run.cancel — Requests cancellation at the next condition boundary export.report Optional branch_id {path} for latest run's Markdown report

For a single run, the condition must match the selected branch's condition. To run all four sample branches, pass conditions: ["C0","C1","C2","C3"] in that order. export.report requires a saved run for that branch.

run.start also accepts adapter_mode: "template"|"record"|"replay", model_manifest, adapter_command, budget (max_calls, max_tokens, optional max_cost_micros), and allow_data_transfer: true. A multi-condition call shares one budget. Record mode needs explicit transfer permission; replay uses the local cassette and no executable. See the adapter contract.

async: true returns promptly. Poll run.status with the returned job_id; its completed and total fields show condition progress. Each status result is a snapshot, so its run list will not change after the response is returned. run.cancel stops before the next condition, without changing sealed story or discourse. Read-only graph/event queries and draft editing remain available while a run is active; canon, fixture, contract, study, and export mutations are refused until it finishes.

docs.title: Blinded study
docs.text:
Method Parameters Result study.plan.save / study.plan.get plan for save Frozen plan, hash, creation time, and optional prior-plan hash study.generate — Three deterministic composition variants for each C0–C3 branch study.metrics Optional branch_id Layer A blocking and Layer B descriptive measures study.ablations Optional branch_id Seven analysis-only ablation descriptions and hashes study.ablations.realize Optional branch_id Seven saved controlled passages, packet/text hashes, and findings; canon unchanged study.export Optional integer seed Public folder, private key path, study ID, passage count study.responses.import study_id and path or responses document Validated batch count; malformed batches make no changes study.report study_id Saved descriptive report, including null and contrary results study.decision_packet study_id Saved hashed evidence packet; human decision remains pending

The public evaluation folder includes an accessible HTML protocol and passages. The condition key lives under study/keys/ and should not be shared with evaluators. See the evaluation procedure.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"error":{"code":-32000,"message":"…","data":{"cmne_code":"E-STORY-001","field_path":"title","next_action":"…","cause":"…"}}}

-32000 wraps a CmneError; -32602 indicates invalid parameters (including a non-object params value); -32700 indicates invalid JSON; -32603 is an internal sidecar error. A non-object request receives E-PROTO-001. The cmne_code gives the domain-specific cause. Unknown methods yield E-RPC-001. See Data contracts and errors.

docs.title: Model adapter contract
docs.text: The desktop and CLI default to the deterministic template. An optional JSON executable can propose story commands or realize prose. The executable is supplied by the researcher; CMNE does not bundle a vendor service or credentials. Every adapter call passes through a call/token/cost budget and a local request/response cassette.

docs.title: Prepare a run
docs.text:
1. Create a JSON manifest with exactly model_name, model_version, prompt_version, integer seed, and decoding. The optional decoding fields are integer temperature_bp, top_p_bp, and max_output_tokens.
  2. Make an executable that reads one JSON request from standard input and writes one JSON response to standard output. Store credentials in its environment or a configuration file excluded from version control. Do not pass credentials in the manifest, command arguments, or output.
  3. Use --allow-data-transfer only after reviewing the fixture and evaluator data for that run. Record mode refuses an adapter call without this flag. Replay mode needs no executable or network access.
{"model_name":"research-adapter","model_version":"1","prompt_version":"scene-v1","seed":33,"decoding":{"temperature_bp":0,"max_output_tokens":512}}

docs.title: Request and response
docs.text:
The input has role (prose or proposal), manifest, and payload. A prose payload contains the filtered scene packet and variant_index. A proposal payload contains current projections, the contract, unresolved goals and contradictions, allowed command types, a limited entity/predicate catalog, branch ID, and expected sequence.

The output must contain only output and usage. usage has nonnegative integer input_tokens, output_tokens, and cost_micros. Prose output is a string. Proposal output is an object with a candidates array of at most 16 entries; each entry has payload, rationale, and expected_effects. Rationales stay in diagnostic proposal records and are never world facts. A proposal changes canon only after accept-proposal sends its payload through the ordinary story command validator.

{"output":"The room was quiet.","usage":{"input_tokens":20,"output_tokens":5,"cost_micros":0}}

docs.title: Record and replay
docs.text:
cmne --json run PROJECT --branch BRANCH --adapter-mode record \
  --adapter-command /path/to/adapter --model-manifest manifest.json \
  --max-calls 5 --max-tokens 10000 --allow-data-transfer

cmne --json run PROJECT --branch BRANCH --adapter-mode replay \
  --model-manifest manifest.json --max-calls 5 --max-tokens 10000

cmne --json propose PROJECT --branch BRANCH --adapter-mode record \
  --adapter-command /path/to/adapter --model-manifest manifest.json \
  --allow-data-transfer
cmne --json accept-proposal PROJECT PROPOSAL_ID --branch BRANCH

The cassette key is the SHA-256 hash of the canonical request. cassettes/<hash>.json stores the request, response, and response hash. Replay validates both hashes and never invokes the executable. A missing or corrupt entry raises E-CASSETTE-001; recording a different response for an existing request is refused. The sixth call under a five-call budget raises E-BUDGET-001 before invoking the adapter and reports spend so far. Adapter failures fall back to the template for prose runs and are recorded as adapter_failure without copying vendor exception text. Budget and cassette errors stop the run.

flowchart LR
  P[Filtered packet or proposal context] --> G[Privacy and budget guard]
  G -->|record| A[JSON adapter executable]
  A --> C[(Canonical cassette)]
  G -->|replay| C
  C --> V[Response shape and integrity validation]
  V --> X[Prose checker or command validator]

The current implementation has contract tests with an offline fake and a subprocess adapter bridge. A specific external model/vendor, cost ceiling, and credential configuration have not been selected for release. Model-generated prose remains a candidate subject to the deterministic checker and human review.

docs.title: Python kernel
docs.text:
Install the project in a virtual environment as described in Install and launch. Imports below use the installed cmne package.

from cmne.project import Project

project = Project.create("/tmp/my-scene", "My scene")
try:
    story = project.append_story("main", {
        "title": "The letter arrives",
        "kind": "action",
        "actor_ids": ["actor_a"],
        "description": "A letter arrives at the door."
    })
    project.append_discourse("main", {
        "title": "Opening",
        "mode": "scene",
        "story_refs": [story["event_id"]],
        "text": "A letter waited at the door."
    })
    result = project.run("main")
    print(result["status"], result["prose"])
finally:
    project.close()

docs.title: Pure functions
docs.text:
cmne.core provides validate_fixture, validate_contract, validate_story_event, validate_discourse_act, replay, build_packet, template_realize, check_realization, canonical, digest, and stable_id. cmne.machines provides weighted strain, crisis assessment, modal revision, and epiphany-candidate functions. cmne.prose provides the ProseRealizer protocol and sentence checker. cmne.study provides analysis-plan, blind-set, response, and report functions. cmne.formula provides validate, evaluate, and EvaluationContext. Validation raises CmneError with code, field_path, and next_action; the sidecar serializes it as RPC error data.

These functions are the current Python interfaces, not a separate network service. For the exact field shapes, see Data contracts.

cmne.adapters provides the ProposalAdapter and ProseAdapter protocols, CommandAdapter, ModelGateway, and manifest validator. The adapter contract describes the executable JSON protocol, privacy opt-in, budget, and cassette replay.

docs.title: Tauri bridge
docs.text:
The Rust shell exposes two commands to the React frontend:

Command Arguments Result rpc_call method: string, params: JSON object Sidecar result value or rejected promise with error string default_sample_path None Documents/CMNE/Mara and Len path 
import { invoke } from "@tauri-apps/api/core";

const project = await invoke("rpc_call", {
  method: "project.sample",
  params: {},
});
const path = await invoke<string>("default_sample_path");

app/src/api.ts wraps invoke in rpc<T>(method, params) and turns serialized sidecar errors into messages containing the CMNE code and field path. It also defines Lens, ViewNode, ViewEdge, ViewGraph, Draft, ProjectSummary, and RunResult TypeScript types.

The Rust bridge permits only methods in its METHODS allow-list, currently the JSON-RPC reference method set. It owns one child sidecar behind a mutex, increments request IDs, checks matching response IDs, and performs the protocol handshake on start. Development uses python3 -m cmne_sidecar.server with PYTHONPATH set to the repository src; the packaged app uses its bundled cmne-sidecar executable. CMNE_SIDECAR_BIN can override the child path. After an unexpected exit or broken pipe, the bridge retries only stateless app.hello, fixture.validate, and contract.validate calls. It returns an uncertain-outcome error for project calls and creates a fresh sidecar on the next request. Reopen and inspect the project before repeating an interrupted mutation; the bridge cannot infer whether that mutation committed before the child stopped.

The shell does not interpret narrative payloads. Validation and storage stay in the Python kernel. The workbench calls run.start with async: true, polls run.status, and can request run.cancel; the sidecar stops before the next condition. The Rust bridge still serializes individual RPC requests, but each background-run request returns promptly so committed-state reads remain available.

docs.title: Design overview
docs.text:
CMNE is a local narrative workbench for a bounded two-actor scene. It separates what happened (story) from how the reader encounters it (discourse), then replays sealed events into actor, world, reader, tension, and style views. A scene packet feeds an offline deterministic realizer. The desktop app is Tauri 2, React, and a Python sidecar.

flowchart LR
  Author --> React[React workbench]
  React --> Tauri[Tauri command bridge]
  Tauri --> Python[Python sidecar and kernel]
  Python --> Store[(Local project folder)]
  Python --> Run[Packet, prose, findings]
  Run --> React

The design pages document implemented behavior. The original _design specifications describe the broader research system. See Current limits before treating a research scenario as available in this build.

Topic Page Narrative entities, revisions, and the C0–C3 comparison Domain model Components and protocol boundary Runtime architecture Deterministic run and checking Pipeline Project layout, integrity, and branches Storage Shipped scope and planned work Roadmap Dated ten-category software review Code review

For user tasks, start with the manual. For callable interfaces, see the API.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
  participant UI as React workbench
  participant Shell as Tauri/Rust
  participant RPC as Python sidecar
  participant Kernel as cmne kernel
  participant Files as Project files
  UI->>Shell: invoke rpc_call(method, params)
  Shell->>RPC: one JSON-RPC request line
  RPC->>Kernel: dispatch and validate
  Kernel->>Files: read/write project state
  Kernel-->>RPC: result or CmneError
  RPC-->>Shell: one JSON-RPC response line
  Shell-->>UI: result or error string

The React UI owns editing interaction and graph presentation. The Rust command rpc_call restricts method names and serializes access to one child process. It starts the Python sidecar from the development virtual environment or bundled executable and performs app.hello. After a child failure, only stateless validation requests are retried automatically; a project request returns an uncertain-outcome error so no write is sent twice. The sidecar speaks line-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 on standard input/output; logs go to standard error. The Python kernel owns narrative validation, storage, replay, packet construction, realization, and checking.

The UI offers seven lenses. Story and Discourse allow drafts; Fixture, Mind, Provenance, Motif, and Pipeline visualize current or derived data. The graph envelope includes nodes and edges with IDs, titles, fields, state, and text alternatives. An outline, inspector, scrubber, strain chart, trace pane, and branch comparison provide other routes through the same data.

docs.text:
Boundary Contract React → Rust Tauri invoke("rpc_call", {method, params}) or default_sample_path Rust → Python One JSON-RPC request/response per newline, protocol major version 1 Sidecar → kernel In-process Python calls over JSON-compatible values Kernel → disk Local project directory, hashed NDJSON streams and atomic JSON writes

The sidecar is stateful: app.hello precedes other calls and one project can be open in a process. The project lock allows one writer. Read the JSON-RPC reference and Tauri bridge for method details.

docs.title: Software code review
docs.text:
The 2026-10-21 review examined the Python kernel and sidecar, the Tauri bridge, the React workbench, tests, build checks, and documentation. The full review in _design records the evidence and remaining gates. These are software scores; the older 100/100 package score assesses the written design.

Category, ranked by current evidence Score / 10 Gate still open Type and API contracts 9 Cross-language contract depth Determinism and sealed history 8 Full invariant and cross-OS vectors Error handling and recovery 8 Packaged GUI crash journey Sidecar and process boundary 8 Real restart and fault matrix Documentation and traceability 8 Full AC/GAC evidence Test behavior and independence 8 Nine separate histories pass; complete epiphany semantics, mutation, and GUI tests remain Code organization and maintainability 7 Large UI/project modules Build and portability 7 Clean-checkout three-OS CI and packages Python coverage and regression depth 7 Branch/mutation and lower-coverage boundaries Workbench usability and accessibility 5 Keyboard, assistive-tech, graph performance, GUI E2E

A 10 means the relevant SRS release gate has passed on supported targets. None has that evidence yet. The review did fix failed project switching, contract changes that could invalidate sealed crises, post-commit command reporting, malformed study and RPC inputs, mutable background status snapshots, automatic replay of uncertain writes, and a stale draft pointer. Nine separate golden histories now check machine outcomes independently of the bundled sample. Seeded properties and model cassette tests extend that evidence. Python passes 103 behavior tests, 89.9% executable-line coverage (3,153/3,509), Mypy, and Ruff; Rust Clippy and its recovery-policy unit test pass. These checks are part of the configured CI, which has not yet run from a clean checkout on all targets.

The roadmap lists the software gates before Milestone 9. Milestone 9 requires human evaluation, independent review, and release sign-off.

docs.title: Story, discourse, and perspectives
docs.text:
The fixture names exactly two actors, entities, initial facts, and optional style. The contract states required/forbidden story conditions, facts that should be clear, questions left open, prose bounds, and a strain threshold. Story events are sealed in sequence; discourse acts select and order references to those events. Replay derives six projections: actor_a, actor_b, environment, tension, reader, and prose_style.

erDiagram
  PROJECT ||--|| FIXTURE : contains
  PROJECT ||--|| CONTRACT : contains
  PROJECT ||--o{ BRANCH : contains
  BRANCH ||--o{ STORY_EVENT : seals
  BRANCH ||--o{ DISCOURSE_ACT : seals
  DISCOURSE_ACT }o--o{ STORY_EVENT : references
  STORY_EVENT ||--o{ INTERPRETATION : records
  BRANCH ||--o{ RUN : produces

The sample Mara and Len is a controlled comparison. C0 reveals a fact; C1 revises a belief; C2 adds a possible situation; C3 changes the concepts used to classify prior events. All share the same first seven story events and diverge later. The question is whether a later change affects how earlier details are understood, even though the sealed past stays intact.

Revision Implemented representation Projection effect Interpretation Claim tied to an observer and earlier story sequence(s) Adds an interpretation and belief to that actor Belief Observer, claim, status, confidence, accessible evidence Replaces that actor's claim status Modal Observer and added scenarios Increments modal model version and appends scenarios Conceptual Observer, concepts, migration map Creates a new conceptual model version with superseded model

This representation supports useful inspection, but it is not yet a complete formal epistemic/modal revision engine. The current formula AST supports tri-state preconditions and bounded syntax; provenance and grounding checks are partial.

docs.title: Temporal relations
docs.text: Story sequence is the order of sealed events. A causal edge must point from an earlier sealed event to a later one. A discourse act can reference any sealed story event and is itself ordered in the discourse stream. A later event's interpretation can target earlier story sequence numbers. The scrubber replays a prefix of story and optionally a prefix of discourse; this lets an author compare the world and the reader's disclosed information at a chosen point.

docs.title: Design invariants
docs.text:
• Exactly two fixture actors, with unique actor/entity IDs.
  • Event stream entries carry stable IDs and integrity hashes; earlier sealed entries are not edited in place.
  • Observation has an observer and an access path; belief revision cites evidence the observer could access.
  • Discourse reveal is grounded in referenced story facts, except when hypothetical/unreliable is explicitly marked.
  • Causal parents are earlier events; a draft causal graph cannot contain cycles.
  • Runs and exports are derived artifacts, separate from sealed canon.

docs.title: Run flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  V[Validate] --> R[Replay]
  R --> RV[Revise]
  RV --> P[Plan]
  P --> PK[Packet]
  PK --> Z[Realize]
  Z --> C[Check]
  C --> Saved[(Run JSON and packet JSON)]

These seven names are recorded in each run's stages. Project.run performs packet construction, deterministic realization, and checks in one operation; stage entries report the outcome, not seven independent worker services. The sidecar can run conditions in a background worker, report completed conditions, and cancel before the next condition. If findings exist, the run marks the responsible stage failed and later stages skipped.

docs.title: Packet content
docs.text: build_packet replays the branch and combines ordered acts with discourse time, focal access, reader state before/after each act, licensed claims, style, forbidden assertions, unresolved questions, voice rules, and word bounds. Story references outside focal access have their descriptions/facts removed from the realizer view. A canonical hash identifies the packet, saved at packets/<packet-hash>.json when running.

docs.title: Realization
docs.text: template_realize joins authored discourse text with blank lines. If an act has no text, it uses referenced story descriptions/titles. The unchanged seeded Mara and Len story can use authored expanded paragraphs; custom projects and edited cues use their actual authored text. This is the default offline path. A researcher-supplied JSON adapter can realize a candidate in record mode with explicit data-transfer permission, or replay a saved response offline.

docs.title: Checks and limits
docs.text:
Check Current behavior Word bounds Counts word-like tokens and compares with contract min/max Forbidden assertions Case-insensitive literal substring search in realized prose Focal access and prose Sentence annotations flag selected unsupported claims, private cognition, named entities, causal assertions, early literal reveals, and explicit open-question resolution Voice Forbidden phrases and sentence-length bounds are deterministic checks Required story conditions Confirms each required condition occurs in grounded story facts Missing content Flags empty story or discourse Disclosure grounding Validated when sealing discourse acts

The checker uses deterministic language rules and optional structured sentence annotations. It is not a general semantic proof: paraphrases can be missed, and figurative language can be ambiguous. The sample's care/avoidance question has an explicit resolution pattern; arbitrary open questions need their own rule or review. Model outputs pass through the same checker; adapter annotations cannot downgrade an unhedged assertion. The manual explains how to read a finding.

docs.text:
This page distinguishes the running app from the broader SRS-033 design. The detailed requirement and scenario checkpoint lives in _design/SRS-033-Implementation-Status.md.

Area Implemented now Planned in the source design Authoring Story/discourse drafts, preview, seal, fork, basic compare, fixture/contract JSON editing Full concept/rule palette editing and richer diff tools State Deterministic replay, six projections, weighted strain/crisis gates, belief/modal/conceptual transitions, provenance traces, motif ledger, nine independent sealed-history fixtures, and seeded property checks Broader formal semantics and full invariant evidence Realization Offline authored text/template, packet and run hashes, JSON adapter bridge, call/token/cost budget, and canonical cassette replay Selected external vendor and release credential configuration Checking Structural invariants and sentence-level checks for selected access, disclosure, resolution, and voice rules Stronger semantic grounding and adversarial corpus coverage Evaluation Individual Markdown export; fixed plans, 12 matched offline variants, blinded set, response import, descriptive report, seven realized controlled ablations, and a hashed generalization review packet Human study, literary interpretation, and signed generalization decision (Milestone 9) Recovery Persistent drafts, project lock, sidecar retry for stateless validation calls only Complete crash recovery and published-run replication

The current checkpoint includes decision records, a 272-ID acceptance inventory, generated JSON Schema/TypeScript contracts, atomic batches, verified snapshots, local hash vectors, weighted crisis logic, study tooling, and adapter cassettes. The local Python suite has 103 tests. Milestones 0–4 remain open where cross-platform, semantic, vendor, or complete acceptance evidence is missing. Revised Milestones 5 and 8 pass their local software gates; Milestones 6 and 7 still need GUI and release evidence. Milestone 9 holds the human study and sign-off. The ten-category software review ranks current code quality separately from the historical written-design score. It records the recent fixes to project switching, contract replacement, post-commit errors, study/RPC validation, background status snapshots, and sidecar retry policy.

Scenario S-04's diagnostic flow is useful today, but a subtle claim can still pass the deterministic checker. S-07–S-09 can be dry-run with synthetic responses; human results are not yet collected. S-10–S-12 now have an adapter/cassette API path; a release vendor and published-run replication test remain open. docs.text:
project.cmne.json
.cmne.lock
fixtures/active.json
contracts/active.json
branches/<branch-id>/story.ndjson
branches/<branch-id>/discourse.ndjson
branches/<branch-id>/evaluation.ndjson
snapshots/<branch-id>.json
drafts/<draft-id>.json
packets/<packet-hash>.json
runs/<run-id>.json
exports/<run-id>.md

The metadata file records the name, active branch, parent, fork sequence, and condition labels where present. Fixture and contract are current JSON documents with content hashes. Story and discourse streams contain one event per line. Drafts are mutable JSON; packets, runs, and exports are generated from sealed data.

docs.title: Event integrity
docs.text:
An event contains stream, branch_id, one-based sequence, schema_version, payload, event_id, and integrity_hash. IDs and hashes come from canonical JSON with sorted keys and SHA-256. On read, the kernel verifies sequence, schema, ID, hash, and duplicate IDs. A same-stream command validates its full event batch before one atomic file replacement; existing sealed lines retain their original bytes. Never edit a sealed stream directly.

The lock records PID, host, and start time. One writer owns it, while a read-only project instance can inspect committed streams. A stale lock is reported and must be cleared explicitly after confirming that its writer stopped. Full replay checks a snapshot against fixture, contract, reducer, event heads, projection data, and content hash; an invalid snapshot is rebuilt by a writer. Snapshot files are caches, not canon. The shipped event schema and reducer are version 2; version-1 story/discourse events gain source_kind: authored in memory while their sealed bytes and IDs remain unchanged. Project metadata remains format version 1.

Fixture and contract edits revalidate sealed events and preconditions before replacing their JSON files. A proposed contract that makes an existing crisis invalid is refused and leaves the old contract bytes intact. A failed switch to another project keeps the current project's lock and state.

docs.title: Fork semantics
docs.text:
flowchart TD
  M[Main: S01 to S07] --> F[Fork at sequence 7]
  F --> A[Branch A: verified prefix plus new suffix]
  F --> B[Branch B: verified prefix plus new suffix]
  A --> RA[Run A]
  B --> RB[Run B]

Forking copies a verified story prefix and the initial contiguous discourse acts whose references remain in that prefix into a new branch. It stops copying discourse at the first act that refers beyond the prefix. The old story suffix becomes editable draft nodes on the new branch. When sealed, those nodes receive new event IDs. branch.compare reports common payload prefix, first divergence, counts unique to each branch, and projection hashes. It does not generate a prose diff.

docs.title: Reproducibility boundary
docs.text: Replay reduces fixture, contract, and selected event prefixes into six projections and content hashes. Integer basis points avoid floating-point state in strain and confidence fields. The run saves the packet hash, projection hashes, realizer ID, stages, prose, findings, adapter spend, and a reproducibility record. Canonical model requests and responses live under cassettes/; replay checks request and response hashes without a network call. This supports local repeatability; published replication and full evaluation provenance remain future work.

Path Purpose mkdocs.yml Navigation, Material theme, Mermaid support, and build paths site/ Markdown source for the documentation docs/ Generated HTML output for GitHub Pages

docs.text: The verified packaging path is an unsigned macOS app. It builds a React frontend, Rust Tauri shell, and PyInstaller Python sidecar. source .venv/bin/activate
