docs.title: User manual: work from a question
docs.text:
This manual starts with a task, shows the action, and then explains the construct behind it. Its structure adapts Robert E. Horn's Information Mapping approach: small, labeled units with one purpose and a presentation suited to the reader's question. The Information Mapping methodology identifies information units and types; its type guide distinguishes concept, structure, process, procedure, principle, and fact.

Label in this manual Reader question Typical form Concept What is it? Short definition and example Structure What parts does it have? Part/function table or diagram Process What happens? Stage/result table Procedure How do I do it? Numbered steps and expected result Principle What rule should guide my choice? Constraint and reason Fact What is true in this release? Specific behavior or limit

docs.title: Task map
docs.text:
Scenario Your question Page S-01 What does the sample do? First run S-02 How do I make my own scene? Build a scene S-03, S-05 How do I revise an interpretation or remove an event safely? Revise and compare S-04 Why did a run fail, and how do I get a passage? Generate and export S-06 What differs between C1 and C3? Read the result S-07–S-09 How do I prepare a blinded study dry run and read responses? Prepare a blinded evaluation S-10, S-13 What happens when a process stops or a draft remains? Troubleshooting

S-07–S-09 have a file-based study dry run; seven controlled ablation passages are saved; recruited human evaluation is still open. S-11 and S-12 have a record/replay adapter API, while a release vendor and published-run replication work remain open; see the roadmap.

docs.title: Principle: separate evidence from interpretation
docs.text: An event records what happened. An interpretation records an observer's reading of it, with a model version and possible references back to earlier events. A discourse act decides what the reader encounters and when. Keeping these distinct lets a later reinterpretation change Mara's understanding without rewriting Len's earlier repair.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Create a bounded local project, record what happens, decide what the reader sees, and seal a runnable scene. This procedure uses the current GUI. For advanced revision fields, use the JSON-RPC API.

docs.title: Fact: current editing surface
docs.text:
The GUI can create a project, edit the fixture and contract as validated JSON, and edit story and discourse drafts. New projects begin with two placeholder actors (actor_a, actor_b) and no entities. Mind and Motif are mostly inspection lenses today. The GUI does not yet provide a palette for adding actors, objects, rules, or full revision operators. Use the Fixture lens JSON editors to rename actors or add entities before writing events; see contracts.

Saving a fixture or contract checks it against every sealed story event and event precondition first. If a new crisis threshold would invalidate an existing crisis, the save is rejected and the prior contract remains in place. A contract is project-wide across branches, so test a conflicting rule in a separate project copy.

docs.title: Procedure: create a project
docs.text:
1. Click the project name in the top bar and choose Create new.
  2. Enter an absolute folder path that does not already contain a CMNE project, and a project name.
  3. Click Create project. The new project opens in Story lens. If you keep the placeholder fixture, use actor_a and actor_b in actor fields.

Result. The folder has project.cmne.json, a fixture, a contract, and a main branch. The new default contract has no required story conditions and permits 0–1100 words.

docs.title: Procedure: set the fixture and contract
docs.text:
1. Open Fixture. Edit Fixture JSON to name the two actors, add entities, or set starting facts. Choose Validate and save fixture. The sidecar checks existing sealed references before replacing it.
  2. Edit Narrative contract JSON to set required and forbidden conditions, questions to leave open, strain weights, and prose_bounds. Choose Validate and save contract. If min_words exceeds max_words, an inline error appears and saving is disabled; the sidecar still performs the full validation.
  3. Read any coded error, cause, and next action in the status message. Correct the JSON or the named field and save again.

Result. The workbench refreshes the validated project summary and graph. Sealed event bytes are not rewritten.

docs.title: Structure: minimum authoring constructs
docs.text: Construct What it stores Authoring choice Fixture Two actors, entities, initial facts, style Choose the cast and objects before sealing events Contract Required/forbidden story claims, open questions, word bounds, strain threshold Decide what the passage must and must not assert Story event Title, kind, participants, observations, optional facts/revisions, strain Say what happened in story time Discourse act Mode, text, focalizer, story references, reveal/withhold Decide when and how the reader encounters an event Draft Editable nodes and edges Work before committing to canon Sealed event Validated event in the NDJSON stream Preserve the branch's history

docs.title: Procedure: add story events
docs.text:
1. Open Story and choose Add event. Select the draft node.
  2. In the inspector, enter a specific Title and Description. Choose an event kind: action, observation, utterance, recollection, decision, revision, or crisis.
  3. Enter actor IDs in Actors. For an observation, enter at least one Observed by ID and choose a perception, testimony, or memory access path. The sidecar rejects an observation without these fields.
  4. Set the strain slider if the event increases or eases pressure. The stored value is an integer from 0 to 10,000 basis points; the UI displays a percentage.
  5. To record causation, select a draft event, click Connect from, then select the target story event. The sidecar checks the connection; a sealed event cannot gain a new causal parent.
  6. Repeat for each beat. Click Seal draft. Correct any field or connection errors reported by the preview, then seal again.

Result. The event or group of draft events is appended to the branch's story stream. Sealed events cannot be edited in place; fork to revise.

docs.title: Procedure: plan discourse
docs.text:
1. Open Discourse and choose Add act. Select the new draft act.
  2. Choose a mode such as scene, summary, memory, or pause. Enter Passage text and select a focalizer or narrator.
  3. Select the act and click Connect from, then select the story event it discloses. This creates a refs edge from the act to the event.
  4. If you use Reveal claims, each claim must match a world_facts value on a referenced story event. The GUI does not expose world_facts editing yet, so leave Reveal empty when using the GUI alone. A claim already revealed cannot later be withheld.
  5. Seal the discourse draft. Add more acts in the order the reader should encounter them, which may differ from story order.

Result. A run can produce prose from the acts' text. For custom projects, the offline realizer joins the authored act text in discourse order; it does not invent missing scenes. Set enough text to satisfy your contract's word bounds.

docs.title: Principle: keep private knowledge out of observed events
docs.text: An observation must name who had access and how. This is a narrow validation rule in the current release. The prose checker does not yet reliably detect every sentence that implies another character's private thought. Write and review the passage accordingly.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Generate and export the passage, then read its findings.

docs.title: Concept — the narrative layers
docs.text: Layer Meaning Sample example Fixture Stable cast, objects, starting facts, style Mara, Len, chair, bowl Contract Conditions and limits for a run Keep a question open; prose word bounds Story Events in causal/chronological sequence Chair rocks; Mara sees a note Discourse Order and manner of telling A later paragraph remembers the chair Projection Derived state after replay Mara's belief, reader disclosure, strain Packet Bounded input to the realizer Ordered acts, grounded facts, limits Run Saved prose and findings A C3 passage and its Check status

docs.title: Structure — story event
docs.text:
A story event has a title and a kind (action, observation, utterance, recollection, decision, revision, or crisis). Optional fields include description, actor/entity IDs, earlier causal parents, world facts, observers, interpretations, revisions, and strain_bp.

For an observation, identify an observer and access_path: perception, testimony, or memory. For a belief revision, point to an earlier event the observer actually observed. A causal parent must already be sealed on that branch.

docs.title: Structure — discourse act
docs.text: A discourse act has a title and a mode: scene, summary, ellipsis, pause, memory, or repetition. story_refs link it to sealed story events. text is its authored narration; focalizer selects a known actor. reveal must be grounded in the referenced events' world facts unless the act is marked hypothetical or unreliable. withhold cannot name a claim already revealed in a previous act.

docs.title: Process — how interpretations change the past
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  A[Earlier sealed event] --> B[Later observation]
  B --> C[Later interpretation targets earlier sequence]
  C --> D[Replay updates actor projection]
  A --> E[Original event stays sealed]

An interpretation records an observer, claim, positive model version, and optional earlier target sequences. It changes the derived mind projection. It does not alter the referenced event. A belief revision records accepted, rejected, or suspended status and confidence in basis points. A modal revision adds possible scenarios; a conceptual revision creates a new model version and migration map. These implemented transitions are basic representations of the richer theory in Domain model.

docs.title: Principle — authoring boundaries
docs.text: Edit Story and Discourse through drafts, then preview and seal. Once sealed, fork to change a story suffix. The other five lenses are read-only views of fixture or derived state. Fixture and contract JSON can be managed through the sidecar API; the current GUI has no direct editors for them.

docs.title: Fact — formula language
docs.text: Preconditions use JSON AST operators atom, not, and, or, implies, necessarily, possibly, believes, suspends, and in_scenario. Evaluation can return true, false, or unknown. The validator limits depth to 16 and nodes to 256. See Data contracts.

docs.title: Prepare and evaluate a blinded comparison — S-07 to S-09
Concept — what the study tests
docs.text:
The four conditions share S01–S07. C0 adds a fact, C1 corrects a belief, C2 admits another possibility, and C3 revises Mara's conceptual model while leaving the central question open. The reader projection and structural measures are simulated and descriptive. Human responses are the evidence for claims about what readers noticed.

The current offline realizer makes three matched composition variants per condition. These are deterministic edits of the same authored prose, not independent model generations. A researcher should inspect all twelve candidates and record any rejected candidates before recruiting readers.

flowchart LR
  A[Save analysis plan] --> B[Generate 3 variants × 4 conditions]
  B --> C[Export randomized public set]
  B --> ABL[Realize seven controlled ablations]
  C --> D[Keep condition key private]
  D --> E[Collect cited-span responses]
  E --> F[Validate and import]
  F --> G[Descriptive report]
  G --> H[Generalization review packet]

docs.title: Procedure — freeze the analysis plan
docs.text:
1. Open the Mara and Len sample in the workbench and expand Evaluation study under Run analysis.
  2. Edit the JSON plan. State hypotheses, the four primary measures, any secondary measures, target sample size and rationale, agreement metric, exclusion rules, and session limit. The example is a template, not a preregistered study decision.
  3. Choose Save or amend plan. The project stores its hash and creation time. A later change creates a linked amendment; the earlier plan remains on disk.

The CLI equivalent is cmne analysis-plan PROJECT plan.json. The plan can use percent_agreement or cohen_kappa.

docs.title: Procedure — export the blinded set
docs.text:
1. Choose Generate 12 matched passages. The workbench saves variants 0–2 for C0–C3 and checks each run.
  2. Choose a randomization seed and select Export blinded set.
  3. Share only the returned public folder. It contains manifest.json, protocol.html, and each passage as plain text and accessible HTML.
  4. Keep the returned key path private. It is stored under <project>/study/keys/, outside the public export folder.

From a terminal:

cmne study-generate /path/to/project
cmne export-evaluation /path/to/project --seed 33

Export returns E-PLAN-001 when no plan exists and E-STUDY-001 when any condition lacks three passing, textually distinct candidates. The public files contain opaque passage IDs and no condition labels.

docs.title: Procedure — collect and import responses
docs.text:
Give evaluators the public protocol.html. It asks for an earlier detail and cited span, preparedness rating, resolution classification, and a paired ranking or no discernible difference. Use pseudonymous evaluator IDs. Respect the plan's session limit.

Save responses in a JSON object with a responses array. Each row needs:

Field Value evaluator_id Pseudonymous ID, 3–48 safe characters passage_id, text_version Values from the public manifest paired_ranking first, second, tie, or not_shown free_response Evaluator's own words cited_spans Array of {start, end, earlier_detail} using character offsets in the plain text confidence_bp Integer from 0 to 10000 no_discernible_difference Boolean preparedness_rating Integer 1–5 resolution_class meaningful, confusing, or neither

Enter the study ID and response JSON path in the workbench, then choose Import responses. Or run cmne responses-import PROJECT STUDY_ID responses.json. The entire batch is checked before it is saved; a malformed row reports a field path and leaves the stored response set unchanged. The private key adds the condition after import.

docs.title: Procedure — read the report
docs.text:
Choose Generate report or run cmne report PROJECT STUDY_ID. The JSON report is saved under <project>/study/reports/. It includes primary measures, C3–C0 contrasts and 95% intervals, inter-rater agreement when repeated ratings exist, candidate and rejection counts, contrary results, and null-result alternatives.

An empty or small response set can produce null estimates or unstable intervals. Percent agreement uses all rater pairs for a passage. Cohen's kappa is reported only when paired passages have exactly two ratings; extra raters produce an explicit not-computable reason. Interpret these as limits of the available data. The report does not certify an epiphany or literary quality.

docs.title: Procedure — inspect ablations and prepare a decision
docs.text:
1. Select the C3 branch and choose Realize seven ablations for this branch. The saved records are under <project>/study/ablations/<branch>/. Each has the changed-stream hash, packet hash, passage text and hash, checker findings, and a link to the baseline text hash. Some deliberately altered passages fail checks; keep those rejections in the audit trail.
  2. After exporting a study, choose Build generalization review packet, or run cmne decision-packet PROJECT STUDY_ID. The packet is saved under <project>/study/decision-packets/ and joins C0–C3 structural measures, ablations, response counts, effects, and null/contrary outcomes.
  3. Treat pending_human_review as a handoff status. The packet does not decide whether the literary hypothesis succeeded or whether the project should generalize. That judgment and release sign-off are Milestone 9.

The CLI ablation command is cmne study-realize-ablations PROJECT --branch C3_BRANCH_ID. It works on copies of the sealed streams and does not alter canon. The sample ablations are controlled authored edits; they are comparison material for review, not independent model generations.

docs.title: Reference — structural checks
docs.text: cmne study-metrics PROJECT --branch ID returns Layer A blocking findings and Layer B descriptive measures, including strain, reinterpretation depth, evidence availability, and motif recurrence. cmne study-ablations PROJECT --branch ID lists seven in-memory changes with stable hashes. cmne study-realize-ablations saves their passages and findings. Both operations leave canon unchanged.

docs.title: S-01 · See Mara and Len run
Concept: the bounded experiment
docs.text:
Mara tries to understand Len's leaving. A repaired chair, a blue bowl, and a note become evidence that can be read in more than one way. The sample contains story events S01–S10 and discourse acts D01–D07. Four branches share S01–S07 and diverge at the interpretation of what Mara has learned.

Condition Change represented in the sample Question to ask while reading C0 A new external fact What does the address settle, and what does it leave open? C1 A belief is rejected Which inference does Mara stop making? C2 Another possibility becomes admissible Can care and departure coexist? C3 A concept divides and remains unresolved Do the chair and bowl change meaning without changing as facts?

These are experimental design conditions, not evidence that one passage is better literature. The present offline sample uses authored prose; it does not call a model.

docs.title: Procedure: run the sample
docs.text:
1. Launch the app. The first launch opens Mara and Len · The chair and the bowl. If another project opens, choose the project name at the top and select Open bundled Mara and Len sample.
  2. In the Story lens, select the chair repair, departure, note, and crisis events. The inspector shows each event's canonical fields.
  3. Click Run C0–C3. Progress reports completed conditions while the Pipeline lens stays available. Cancel run stops before the next condition. The completed run records seven stages for each condition.
  4. Choose a C3 branch in the left sidebar. In Latest Run, open Read generated passage. Read the final paragraphs about the chair and bowl.
  5. Switch to C1 and read its passage. Use Compare branches for the shared prefix and first diverging sequence.

Result. Each seeded condition yields a deterministic passage of roughly 800 words and a saved run. A previous short run record remains until you run again after installing an updated build.

docs.title: Structure: seven lenses
docs.text: Lens Main question Current use Fixture Who and what are present? Inspect actors and objects; edit fixture and contract JSON Story What happened? Draft, seal, fork, inspect causal and retrospective edges Discourse In what order is it told? Draft telling acts and connect them to story events Mind What does an actor believe or consider possible? Inspect basic belief, scenario, model, and interpretation nodes Provenance Which event supports a claim? Inspect a basic evidence/claim graph Motif Where do marked objects recur? Inspect basic appearances of the chair and bowl Pipeline What did a run record? Inspect completed stage status per condition

docs.title: Process: story versus telling
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    subgraph StoryTime[Story order]
      S1[S01 Chair repaired] --> S5[S05 Len leaves] --> S7[S07 Note names dates] --> S9[S09 Mara revises]
    end
    subgraph TellingOrder[Discourse order]
      D1[D01 Rocking chair] --> D2[D02 Ordinary reason] --> D3[D03 Note found] --> D4[D04 Chair remembered] --> D6[D06 Meanings held]
    end
    D4 -. refers to .-> S1
    D1 -. refers to .-> S5
    D6 -. refers to .-> S9

The chart shows why the reader can meet the effect before learning the cause. Domain model and theory explains the distinction in more detail.

docs.title: Generate and export a passage — S-04
Concept — generation in this release
docs.text: A run reads the selected branch's sealed story and discourse, builds a scene packet, assembles prose with the offline deterministic realizer, and checks the result. It does not call a language model. A run saves its result separately from the sealed events; running again does not edit canon.

docs.title: Process — from plan to report
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  A[Sealed story and discourse] --> B[Scene packet]
  B --> C[Offline realization]
  C --> D[Sentence, grounding, voice and contract checks]
  D --> E[Saved run JSON]
  E --> F[Markdown export]

docs.title: Procedure — generate the sample
docs.text:
1. Open Mara and Len and select a C0–C3 branch.
  2. Select Run scene for that branch, or Run C0–C3 for all four sample conditions. The workbench shows progress while committed state remains readable; Cancel run stops at the next condition boundary.
  3. Read the passage and run status in the passage/pipeline views. For all four, select each branch to inspect its own passage.
  4. If the status is failed, read the finding and correct the named story, discourse, or contract issue. Fork first if the correction changes a sealed event.
  5. Run again. The newest run is the one used by export for the selected branch.

docs.title: Procedure — export the story
docs.text:
1. Select the branch whose passage you want.
  2. Run that branch at least once.
  3. Choose Export report in the workbench.
  4. Open the returned Markdown file at <project>/exports/<run-id>.md in any text or Markdown editor. The report contains the project title, run ID, status, passage, and findings.

The export is a Markdown report. For a plain story, copy the text under Passage. The run's complete machine-readable record remains at <project>/runs/<run-id>.json.

docs.title: Procedure — generate from the command line
docs.text:
source .venv/bin/activate
cmne run "/path/to/project" --branch main

The CLI prints run JSON, including prose, status, and findings. It does not create the Markdown report; use the desktop Export report action or the sidecar's export.report.

docs.title: Principle — writing a custom scene
docs.text: For a new project, the realizer joins nonempty discourse text in discourse order, separated by blank lines. If an act has no text, it falls back to the descriptions or titles of its referenced story events. Write the desired narration in the discourse acts and use story_refs to keep each act tied to sealed events. The 700–1,100-word authored expansion belongs only to the unchanged Mara and Len seed; an edited cue or a new project uses its own text.

docs.title: Fact — what the checker tests
docs.text: The implemented checker records sentence annotations and deterministic findings for word bounds, forbidden assertions, some unsupported claims and entities, causal claims, another actor's private cognition in close focalization, premature literal disclosures, explicit resolution of the sample's open question, and voice limits. Its language rules are conservative and can miss paraphrases or misclassify a sentence. Read the passage yourself for voice, continuity, and grounding. See Read the result.

docs.title: Concept — four different outputs
docs.text: Output What it answers Where to find it Passage What does the reader see? Passage view; prose in run JSON; exported report Findings and stages Did the current checks pass? Pipeline view; findings, stages, and status in run JSON Projection What does the engine derive at this point? Mind, Provenance, Motif, strain views; scrubber; scrub.projection Trace What supports this selected story event? Trace details; trace.query

docs.title: Procedure — read the sample output
docs.text:
1. Select C0 and read the passage in discourse order. Notice how the chair and bowl recur while the ending leaves the central question open.
  2. Select C1, C2, then C3. Compare the interpretation of earlier events, not only the final action. C1 changes a belief, C2 adds a possible scenario, and C3 changes the categories Mara uses.
  3. In Story, inspect the causal chain and strain values. In Discourse, inspect which story event each act references, what it reveals, and what it withholds.
  4. Scrub to an earlier story sequence and compare the actor and reader projections with the final state. Discourse can point back to an earlier event; telling order is independent of story order.
  5. Open Trace on a story event. Read its causal parents, observers, disclosures, and later interpretations. A later interpretation may target an earlier sequence without rewriting that event.
  6. Check Pipeline and the findings list. passed means the implemented checks found no violation; it is not a literary quality score.

docs.title: Structure — run JSON
docs.text:
{
  "run_id": "run_…",
  "branch_id": "branch_…",
  "conditions": ["C3"],
  "packet_hash": "…",
  "prose": "The passage…",
  "findings": [],
  "stages": [{"condition": "C3", "stage": "Check", "status": "passed"}],
  "projection_hashes": {"actor_a": "…", "reader": "…"},
  "status": "passed",
  "realizer": "deterministic-template-v2"
}

The actual run also contains run_sequence, matched_variant_index, candidate sentence annotations, repair_first, and all seven stage entries. Hashes identify packet and projection content; they are useful for comparing repeatable runs, not for interpreting the prose.

docs.title: Principle — a finding is a diagnostic
docs.text: E-PROSE-WORDS means the generated word count is outside the contract's bounds. E-PROSE-PRIVATE flags a close-focalized assertion about another actor's private cognition; E-PROSE-RESOLUTION flags an explicit answer to the sample's open question. E-VOICE-PHRASE and E-VOICE-LENGTH name style violations. E-RUN-CONTRACT means a required story fact is absent; E-RUN-EMPTY and E-RUN-PLAN mean story or discourse is missing. The finding's layer and optional sentence_index identify where to repair first. Troubleshooting gives recovery steps.

docs.title: Fact — what the strain chart shows
docs.text: For events with strain_components_bp, the chart plots the weighted integer score from contradiction, unexplained evidence, failed prediction, repair complexity, and identity/goal cost. Older sealed events retain their historical strain_bp for replay. This is a modeled value, not a measurement of reader emotion. Telling tension is currently a simple function of withheld claims. Use these numbers to inspect design choices, not as external evaluation.

docs.title: S-03, S-05, S-06 · Revise and compare
Concept: three levels of revision
docs.text:
The Mara/Len conditions isolate different changes. Belief revision changes the status of one claim; modal revision adds a possible scenario; conceptual revision changes the model's vocabulary or interpretation map. The current kernel implements basic transitions for all three, but the full formal operators and revision planner in the target design are not built.

Condition In the sample What remains unchanged C1 belief Mara rejects “The repairs are care.” Earlier chair and bowl events C2 modal Mara admits “care and departure coexist” as a scenario. Earlier facts and their event IDs C3 conceptual Mara's model moves to v2; care maps to care and avoidance, with unresolved terms. Earlier story events; new interpretation records point back to S01 and S02

docs.title: Procedure: fork a sealed event
docs.text:
1. In Story, select the sealed event where the alternative should begin.
  2. Click Fork from here and name the branch. The new branch keeps the sealed prefix before that event and opens draft copies of the selected event and its suffix.
  3. Edit the draft copies in the inspector, add or remove draft nodes, and check their causal connections.
  4. Click Seal draft. The source branch remains intact; the new branch gets its own suffix.
  5. Run the new branch and compare it with the source branch.

Result. The branch comparer reports shared prefix length, first diverging sequence, suffix counts, and projection hashes. It does not yet show the designed graph diff overlay.

docs.title: Process: safe alternative history
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    P[S01–S07 shared sealed prefix] --> A[S08–S10 original branch]
    P --> B[Editable suffix draft]
    B --> C[Validate and seal new branch]
    A --> D[Compare projections]
    C --> D

S-05 example. To ask whether the chair's rocking matters, select the event where it appears, fork, remove its draft copy, and repair later references or preconditions before sealing. The old branch remains available for comparison. The current editor does not provide a one-click visual diff.

docs.title: Procedure: compare C1 and C3
docs.text:
1. Run C0–C3 from the seeded sample.
  2. Select C1 in the left branch list. Click Compare branches and choose C3.
  3. Read the shared prefix and first difference in the comparison panel.
  4. Switch between branches in Mind and Story. On C3, inspect the model v2 node and the retrospective links to S01/S02. In C1, inspect the rejected belief.
  5. Read each passage and note what changed for the character, then what changed for the reader. Read the result explains the limits of that comparison.

docs.title: Principle: an interpretation is not a new fact
docs.text: Mara can reinterpret the chair repair under model v2 while S01 still says the same thing happened. A different interpretation may change the significance of an event without editing the event's canon. Keep that distinction when writing the prose and when comparing conditions.

docs.title: Fact: sample prose on edited branches
docs.text: The long authored expansion is used only when the Mara/Len fixture and story still match a seeded condition and its discourse cues are unchanged. If canon changes, the offline realizer uses the branch's authored discourse text. This prevents the seed's prepared prose from describing a different event as if it were still true.

docs.title: Procedure — a run failed
docs.text:
1. Read the finding code and message in the run view or saved runs/<run-id>.json.
  2. For E-RUN-EMPTY, seal a story event. For E-RUN-PLAN, seal a discourse act that references story.
  3. For E-RUN-CONTRACT, add the required world fact to a story event, or correct the contract if the requirement was wrong.
  4. For E-PROSE-WORDS, edit the discourse text or the contract bounds. For E-PROSE-FORBIDDEN, revise the authored text and run again.
  5. If the correction changes a sealed event, fork before editing. Export the new run after it passes.

docs.title: Procedure — a draft did not seal
docs.text:
1. Keep the draft open and run its preview validation.
  2. Follow the error's field_path: check title, actor IDs, story references, causal edges, observation access, and disclosure grounding.
  3. Correct the draft and preview again. A rejected seal returns errors and does not emit events.
  4. Seal after preview accepts it. Draft JSON persists in <project>/drafts/ until sealed or deleted; after an interrupted session, reopen the project and inspect the recovered draft. The workbench can find the newest draft for the branch and lens on disk even if its local-storage pointer was lost.

docs.title: Principle — preserve project integrity
docs.text:
Do not hand edit sealed NDJSON streams. The engine verifies event IDs, hashes, sequence, and schema when reading them. A second writer receives E-LOCK-001; close the first app/process before reopening the project. Back up the whole project directory when sharing or archiving a branch.

If the app reports a stale lock, confirm the former writer has stopped, then clear it through project.clear_stale_lock or Project.clear_stale_lock(path) before reopening. A read-only open can inspect committed history while another process owns the writer lock. Never clear a lock for a running process or another host.

docs.title: Procedure — sidecar stopped during a project operation
docs.text:
1. Read the error. An outcome unknown message means the child stopped before the shell could confirm whether the operation committed.
  2. Reopen the project. If its old writer left a stale lock, confirm the child stopped and clear that lock explicitly.
  3. Read the relevant event stream, draft, contract, or run record before repeating the action. A failed project switch keeps the previous open project; a failed contract edit leaves its old bytes intact.
  4. Repeat only work that is absent from the saved project. The shell automatically retries only stateless validation calls.

docs.title: Fact — current recovery scope
docs.text: Saved drafts and sealed streams survive a normal process interruption. The optional JSON adapter records failure without vendor exception text and falls back to the template on an unavailable prose adapter. Its call, token, and optional cost limits stop additional calls with E-BUDGET-001; cassette replay works offline. The desktop still defaults to the template and has no bundled model vendor. Background runs can be cancelled before the next condition; a currently executing condition finishes first and sealed events remain intact. The roadmap identifies further recovery work.
